To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spindle-burst oscillations are generated by a network of cortical neurons that are reciprocally connected with each other and the thalamus and are capable of producing a variety of oscillatory patterns, including spindle-burst oscillation, gamma oscillation, and delta oscillation.

the spindle bursts of the neonatal rat barrel cortex in vivo are generated by a network mechanism that involves a combination of local inhibitory and excitatory synaptic interactions, and that the spindle bursts are not generated by intrinsic properties of individual cortical neurons.

1) the rat barrel cortex in vivo network generates spontaneous spindle-burst oscillations, and 2) the mechanisms of spindle-burst oscillation generation are similar to those of spindle-burst generation in the neonatal rat hippocampus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the spontaneous spindle-burst activity in vivo in the barrel cortex.
the mechanisms of spindle-burst oscillations in the neonatal rat barrel cortex in vivo.
the mechanisms that control the generation of oscillations in the developing brain.

the mechanisms responsible for the genesis of the spindle-burst oscillations are unknown.
the spindle-burst network mechanism is not fully understood, and that the current understanding is based on a combination of experimental and theoretical evidence.

the spindle-burst oscillations are generated by the interaction between the intrinsic membrane properties of the cortical pyramidal cells and the synaptic inputs from the thalamic afferents and the local recurrent excitatory connections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that a simple model of the barrel cortex, consisting of only two excitatory and one inhibitory cell, is sufficient to reproduce a large number of the features of the barrel cortex network.
we have demonstrated the existence of an intrinsic oscillatory mechanism in the barrel cortex in vivo that is capable of generating spindle bursts.
the network of the barrel cortex in vivo is a complex system that is able to generate and maintain a wide variety of different rhythms, which are all based on the same network mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not a passive recipient of sensory information but rather actively shapes and organizes sensory information.
we found a new way of controlling the brain.
the barrel cortex is not a homogeneous structure, but rather is composed of a number of distinct subnetworks.
